t: You're on Colvestone Crescent, a street in Hackney, and this is where Dorothy Levitt was born in 1882. She became the first British woman racing driver, and she held the world's first water speed record as well as the women's world land speed record. She also wrote books about motoring and taught Queen Alexandra and the royal princesses to drive. In 1905 she drove a De Dion-Bouton from London to Liverpool and back over two days, and the press called her the Fastest Girl on Earth.
